stories.title: Attacks and blockade enforcement around Hormuz
stories.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued into November. Over the weekend crew abandoned a tanker in Hormuz, US forces struck a bulker in the Gulf of Oman, Iranian media attributed blasts in southern Iran to Iranian military activity, and Houthi forces hit Saudi Aramco's headquarters building.
stories.why_it_matters: Hull strikes, crew abandonment and armed enforcement raise war-risk premiums and crew-safety objections for Arabian Gulf liftings, shrinking the pool of willing owners and supporting tanker earnings.
stories.latest: Seatrade reports crew abandoned a tanker in Hormuz and the US struck a bulker in the Gulf of Oman; Iran and the US both reported shipping hit; Houthi forces struck Saudi Aramco's headquarters building.
sources: Crew abandon tanker in Hormuz, US strikes bulker in Gulf of Oman
Iran Suggests Blasts Are Not US Attacks As Both Sides Report Ships Hit
Houthi Forces Hit Saudi Aramco's Headquarters Building

stories.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
stories.what: US sanctions have expanded across Cuban maritime and energy entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks, while analysts describe the dark fleet as a parallel fleet that has tripled in size since 2022.
stories.why_it_matters: Registry fraud, AIS spoofing and blocked-property designations force charterers, insurers and class societies to re-verify documentation and positions, pushing tonnage out of mainstream trades and tightening compliant tanker supply.
stories.latest: ARACON heard that 25% of the internationally trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list.
sources: ARACON: 25% of the internationally-trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list

stories.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
stories.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, and Russia says its forces hit three cargo vessels it claims were carrying military goods for Ukraine, along with two electricity substations.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
stories.latest: Russia said overnight strikes hit three cargo vessels and two electricity substations.
sources: Russia Says It Hit Three Cargo Ships In Black Sea

stories.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
stories.what: Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG even as VLCC traffic declined, with Red Sea traffic up and Arabian Gulf waiting elevated. Iraq now says it has reached understandings with the US to export oil through Hormuz via a lane near Oman.
stories.why_it_matters: Transit counts, routing lanes and waiting times determine voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
stories.latest: Iraq's foreign minister said Baghdad has understandings with Washington allowing Iraqi oil exports through Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman.
sources: Iraq Has Reached Understandings With US To Allow Oil Exports Through Hormuz

stories.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
stories.what: A contract standoff involving about 250 security workers threatens operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals, while dockworkers have struck across Europe and beyond over arms shipments.
stories.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.

stories.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
stories.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
stories.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.
